chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Mu'awiya ibn Wahb, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Whichever believer visits a sick believer in the morning, seventy thousand angels escort him; and when he sits, mercy overwhelms him and they seek forgiveness for him until evening. And if he visits him in the evening, he shall have the like of that until the morning.

key_terms.اسْتَغْفَرُوا لَهُ: they sought forgiveness for him — the angels interceding on the visitor's behalf
key_terms.شَيَّعَهُ: escort/accompany — used for the angels accompanying the visitor out of honor
key_terms.عَادَ: visited the sick (iyada) — a recommended act in Islamic law
key_terms.غَمَرَتْهُ الرَّحْمَةُ: overwhelmed by mercy — divine mercy enveloping the visitor while seated

ai.seo_question: What reward does a believer receive for visiting a sick Muslim in the morning according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) describes the immense spiritual reward awaiting a believer who visits a sick fellow believer: seventy thousand angels accompany the visitor and continuously seek God's forgiveness on his behalf for the entire duration until evening. The reward doubles if the visit is made in the evening, with the angels' intercession lasting until morning. This teaching, delivered to his companion Mu'awiya ibn Wahb, would have been understood by the early Shia community as a powerful incentive to fulfil a beloved social duty within the brotherhood of believers.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Muawiya Bin Wahab, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Whichever Believer visits a (sick) Believer in the morning, seventy thousand Angels would escort him. So when he sits, the Mercy would overwhelm him, and they would seek Forgiveness for him until evening; and if he visits him in the evening, there would be for him the like of that until the morning’.
en.sarwar: 8. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Mahbub from Mu‘awiyah ibn Wahab who has said the following: “Abu ’Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that

if a believing person visits a believing patient in the morning, seventy thousand angels escort him. When he sits down, mercy covers him altogether until nightfall. If he visits in the evening, similar things happen for him until the next morning.”
